messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — routing overload in us-west-2 affecting hosted-api. Mitigation completed (rolling restart + scale fixes). Full status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3054321000. Postmortem in progress. Paged: @tess-oncall @jamal

tess-oncall: ack — restarted the inference pool and cleared the compile backlog. Capacity back to normal. Observed KV-cache warmup ~6m which explains a short tail.

jamal: handing off to CS. Live-impact summary for customers: some requests returned 500/429 between 15:43–15:55 UTC (~12m). Error rate peaked ~28% for that window. Root cause triage points to an autoscaler policy regression.

maria-cs: Drafting customer-facing note. Proposed copy below — please comment quickly so I can send to legal and hit the status page: 

```
Hi <Customer>,\n\nWe experienced an incident on 2026-03-18 that impacted some requests to the Redwood hosted API in the us-west-2 region. Between 15:43–15:55 UTC a subset of requests for model variants (gpt-redwood-small, gpt-redwood-medium) experienced increased errors (5xx/429).\n\nWhat we fixed: rolling restart of the inference pool, adjusted autoscaler policy, and increased compile worker capacity to prevent backlog.\n\nCustomer impact: some requests failed or were throttled for up to ~12 minutes. If you saw increased errors or reduced throughput during that window, we will proactively open a ticket and offer a service credit for the impacted interval.\n\nNext steps we are taking: postmortem with preventative actions, monitoring improvements to detect similar compile backlogs, and a permanent autoscaler policy fix (PR infra#1423).\n\nIf you want details about whether your account was affected, reply to this thread or open a support ticket and we’ll provide an impact summary.\n\nSincerely,\nRedwood Customer Success\n```

kevin-csm: LGTM. Two asks: 1) include link to the status page in the email, 2) propose an explicit credit offer (suggest 10% of billed usage during the impacted window) so CS can close faster. Also we should list which customers were actually routed to the affected pool — @tess-oncall can you confirm affected account set? :thumbsup:

tess-oncall: confirmed affected model variants: gpt-redwood-small, gpt-redwood-medium in us-west-2. Autoscaler misapplied a CPU limit during a config roll which caused compile worker backlog under burst. Mitigation: reverted the config change, bumped compile worker target, and added a guard to the autoscaler. PR reference: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/pulls/1423.

maria-cs: sending to legal for quick review. Plan: publish status page update first, then send customer email at 2026-03-18 17:00 PDT unless legal asks for changes. Also will offer the 10% credit and include instructions to request it or let us auto-apply where possible.

jamal: timeline for the internal postmortem (so CS can include a concise timeline):
```
15:40 UTC — anomaly detected, error rate rising.\n15:43 UTC — paging alert to oncall.\n15:44–15:50 UTC — triage: identified compile backlog + autoscaler config drift.\n15:50 UTC — rolling restart triggered on inference pool.\n15:55 UTC — error rate returned to baseline, KV-cache warm completed by 16:01.\n16:05 UTC — mitigation confirmed stable, incident marked resolved.\n```

kevin-csm: thanks — add a short note in the email that we’ll provide a per-account impact summary on request. Who will own opening those tickets? @maria-cs or should SRE tagianate?

maria-cs: CS will open tickets for customers we proactively identify; for others we’ll include a form link. I’ll coordinate with ops for the raw request logs needed to generate account-level impact.

sre-bot: Postmortem doc created: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/3054321000. Owner: @jamal. Follow-ups assigned in doc: infra#1423 (autoscaler guard), infra#1428 (compile worker autoscaling test), observability#210 (error-rate alert sensitivity).

maria-cs: perfect — I’ll update the status page now and queue the email. Will post final customer list once I have the logs from ops. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. :pray:
